subject: Discovery recap: Sable Tech private hosting requirements & next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@sabletech.com>, Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@sabletech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Sable Tech — discovery recap and proposed next steps

Hi Ari / Rachel — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ll keep this tight.

Primary pain points you called out
- Production latency spikes during batch ingest windows causing customer-facing errors (99p tail spikes, particularly for large context prompts).
- Data residency and regulatory constraints: PII / medical-adjacent datasets need strict access controls and on-prem or VPC-only deployments.
- Key management: must be customer-managed keys (CloudHSM or HSM-backed KMS) and no plaintext keys stored in a vendor-managed vault.
- Network: limited outbound egress from private environment; strict IP allowlists and no public internet access for model weights during runtime (can be staged via approved channels).

Current stack you described
- Ingest + preproc runs on-prem in GCP dedicated racks; primary backend is C++ microservices.
- Model-serving candidates: on-prem GPUs with limited maintenance windows; prefer reserved capacity model.

Success criteria you want for a pilot
- Private/VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS in place.
- Demonstrable 99p tail latency <= 200ms for single-turn generation under target QPS for the pilot workload.
- No outbound model weight downloads during runtime; all artifacts staged via approved, audited process.
- Audit logs and token-level observability for prompts and responses for compliance review.

Attachments I received from you in the call: sable-network-sketch.pdf (high level diagram) and a data classification spreadsheet — I attached both to the Drive folder (link below).

Proposed immediate next steps (owner / timing)
1) Tech deep dive (Redwood infra + on-prem installer options) — target week of Jul 5. Owner: Marissa Cole (cc’d) to run the session and bring runtime engineer.
2) KMS/Kerberos details: Sable to confirm preferred HSM provider (CloudHSM vs on-prem HSM) and compliance requirements — Owner: Ari / Rachel; due Jul 6.
3) Procurement intro & NDA redlines (if needed) — Ben Carter to loop in procurement contact.
4) Provide sample workload and a 24-hour trace window for us to run a cost/latency estimation — Owner: Sable; requested by Jul 9.

Next meeting: I’ll send a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive after Marissa confirms availability. If any of the bullets above are incorrect or missing, please flag and I’ll update.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bSableTechDiscovery

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@sabletech.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@sabletech.com>, procurement@sabletech.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sable Tech — discovery recap and proposed next steps

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming items and adding a few clarifications from our side:

Clarifications / constraints
- KMS: we will require customer-managed keys via CloudHSM for the pilot. No vendor-managed key material in production.
- Air-gap / verification: for any model artifacts staged into our private environment, we require checksums and signing; transfer must be over our secure transit process (SFTP or private peering).
- Egress: telemetry can be sent to a central observability endpoint but only over a pre-approved, authenticated channel. No external calls that could leak raw prompts.
- Maintenance windows: restricted to 2–4am local time; any patching that could impact compute must be scheduled with 72-hour notice.

Pilot success criteria (slightly refined)
- Security: KMS + attestable artifact transfer + audit logs for every inference request.
- Performance: 99th percentile latency <= 200ms under pilot QPS (we’ll share the 24-hour trace Ari referenced).
- Ops: Ability to roll back model version within 30 minutes if behavior regressions are detected.

Procurement note: procurement@sabletech.com — please expect Ben’s note; we generally want a two-step process: 1) mutual NDA / SOW for pilot, 2) procurement PO on pilot completion.

We’ll aim to have the 24-hour trace and the list of allowed IPs/peers by Jul 6. Let me know if you need anything else before the tech session.

—Rachel
Rachel Lin
Head of Platform Security | Sable Tech
[Signed as: Rachel Lin, Office: +1 415-555-0193]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@sabletech.com>, Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@sabletech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sable Tech — discovery recap and proposed next steps

Appreciate the clarifications, Rachel — all noted and we’re aligned on KMS + artifact signing/checksums and restricted telemetry.

Marissa — can you confirm availability for a 90-minute technical deep-dive the week of Jul 5? Prefer morning PDT windows (9–11am) but we’re flexible. For the session we’ll plan to cover:
- Installer options (VPC-only vs fully air-gapped on-prem bundle)
- KMS integration patterns (CloudHSM, HSM-backed KMS, key rotation flow)
- Network requirements and required ports/IPs for the pilot
- Observability: token-level audit logs and redaction options
- Rollout & rollback flows (canary, A/B, automatic fallback)

Ben — please introduce procurement contact to Rachel and Ari and share our standard pilot SOW template.

Ari / Rachel — once Marissa confirms, I’ll send a detailed agenda and a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Sean

Hi Rachel / Ari — thanks, looking forward to the deep-dive. I can run a session on Tue Jul 6 at 10:00am PDT (60–90 mins). Agenda draft below; please confirm and share the 24-hour trace + allowed IP ranges beforehand.

Draft agenda
1) 10:00–10:15 — Quick intro and goals review (Sean)
2) 10:15–10:40 — Installer and deployment paths: VPC-only, private control plane, and air-gapped bundle (Marissa)
3) 10:40–11:00 — KMS/HSM integration patterns and key lifecycle (runtime & rotation)
4) 11:00–11:20 — Network architecture: required ports, IPs, peering and artifact staging flows
5) 11:20–11:30 — Observability, audit logs, and rollback scenarios

Pre-reads / asks before the call (so we can prepare concrete config samples)
- Please upload the 24-hour trace and the list of allowed IP addresses to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bSableTechDiscovery
- Share preferred HSM vendor details and any compliance checklists (SOC2 / HIPAA snippets) you need us to satisfy

I’ll include one of our runtime engineers and the private deployment lead. If this time works for you I’ll send the calendar invite and a short confluence link with examples of the installer configs.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
